rendered:
Temperature and time: the separated cathode powder was calcined calcined in air at 600 °C for 2 h[1]. The stated purpose was to remove the surface coatings and the conductive carbon black (CB) that remained on the powder.

Why this temperature: the TGA-DTG data show an organic coating layer with a weight loss of ~3.3 wt% loss at ~350 °C[2] and CB with a weight loss of ~4.1 wt% loss at ~550 °C[3]. The authors state that both can be removed by calcining in air at 600[4] °C, so that temperature lies above both decomposition regions. After calcination, the XRD patterns of the reclaimed powder were nearly identical[5] to those of the cathode rejects, with no impurity phases, indicating the calcination left the layered NMC622 structure intact.

The document gives no separate rationale for the hold time; it is reported only as part of the calcination condition.
